# Formal representation

Step 04 derives variable domains and compatibility rules from the canonical
DAG. Its main outputs are `output/rules/VARDOM.dat`, `RULES.dat` and
`record_layout.csv`; `vardom.csv` and `rules_objects.rds` support inspection.
SSPICE uses VOR and VXOR for logical groups and does not generate `STRUTT.dat`
or `LISTE.dat`.

```{r rules}
source(file.path("scripts", "04_create_VARDOM_and_RULES.R"))
stopifnot(all(file.exists(file.path(config$rules_output_dir,
                                    c("VARDOM.dat", "RULES.dat", "record_layout.csv")))))
```

# Validating the theory

Step 05 uses the DAG, `RULES.dat` and item mapping to validate empirical
properties of the induced Horn theory. Closure and minimality checks help
assess whether the formal implications reflect the intended dependencies.
Sampled tests are governed by `n_random_closure_tests`, `max_seed_size` and
the configured seed: interpret their results together with these settings.

```{r horn}
source(file.path("scripts", "05_validate_horn_theory.R"))
```

If routing metadata change, regenerate the DAG, domains and rules before
interpreting a new validation.

# Domains and representation limits

The routing format distinguishes equidistant categories, quantitative
intervals, string presence and numeric codes without value-specific branching.
These conventions are described in
[Building the routing file](routing-02b.html). Check that the exported domains
and item mapping match the intended specification. The absence of path errors
does not establish the validity of every observed value. Passing sampled
closure tests is not, by itself, an exhaustive proof over every possible subset.

# Mapping at export

Supply the same mapping used for record checks to the RULES and VARDOM
generators. They translate structural categories back to observed codes:
for example, a jump associated with routing code 20 can appear in a rule as
`CHOICE(21)` when observed 21 maps to structural 20. The categorical VARDOM
domain likewise lists the observed codes. The executable example in
[Item mapping](item-mapping-02c.html) checks both exports against explicit
expected values.
